newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina submits labour reform to Congress.
newsitem.headline: Argentina submits labour reform to Congress.

text.p: Argentine Labour Minister Armando Caro Figueroa submitted the government's key labour reform project to the lower house of Congress on Monday and called on unions to discuss it, private news agency DyN reported.
Caro Figueroa passed the controversial project to the Chamber of Deputies' majority leader Jorge Matzkin of the governing Peronist Party.
The project, which seeks more flexible labour laws, is being vehemently opposed by unions and many legislators of the Peronist Party and the opposition.
Last week, unions carried out a 36-hour general strike against the government, partly to protest the project which they believe will reduce workers' rights and wages.
Caro Figueroa called on Argentina's main labour group, the CGT, to initiate negotiations "during the course of the week" to sort out differences over labour reform.
President Carlos Menem has recently said more flexible labour laws would be a prime way to fight unemployment, currently at 17.1 percent.
He also argued that more modern labour laws would allow workers in the black market to regularise their situation.
